notes.title: Free Hunt
notes.content:
Hi Hunters,

I'm excited to announce the addition of a free hunt mode to Public Land Hunter. This is a game mode for players to have a casual experience on a larger map without the pressure of a clock. Please see below for details. 

Added:

- Free hunt mode where players can enter a larger map with no time limit and hunt all species except for ducks. This was a common request from players who wanted to have a relaxing time with the game instead of feeling the pressure of the clock. This really resonated with me since a game should be fun and not stressful. Players can still challenge themselves with all the timed hunts but this is a way for players to kick back with something more casual when they just feel like shooting a few things. All kills in this mode count towards unlocks in the cabin. With the removal of a time limit the deer patterning is a little different. Instead of bedding deer will wander onto the map to feed and then wander off. You can still target the acorns they are feeding on but to help you can also now press the trigger when the binos are on a deer to call it in towards you. Note - the deer caller is only available in free hunt mode.

- Pond fishing game in the free hunt. Locate the small pond near the entrance to the free hunt and play a simple fishing game to relax. 10 fish in a row earns the player a new outfit.

- New NPC Gator. Gator is the resident expert and will now allow the player to either skip or reset the intro tasks. This serves two purposes. One, is to allow players that don't want to be content gated to jump to having everything unlocked. The other, is to fix and glitches in progress players experienced after the last patch. The previous patch opened up the ability for the task progression to break when selecting certain weapons or mini games ahead of schedule. If a player is currently missing an NPC or access to a weapon (except the scoped rifle, this is still unlocked from trophy buck kills) then they can speak to Gator to either restart the tasks or just jump to everything being unlocked. Note, this has no effect on kill counts for unlocks.

Bug Fixes:

- Aiming while accessing the computer will no longer cause a crash
- Players can no longer access the weapons in the cabin ahead of time, subsequently breaking task progression
- Corrected a few sound errors
- Removed two lines of code that were causing a graphical glitch

notes.title: Hotfix: March 7
notes.content:
4 Bug Fixes and a small change to the fishing camera (testing it out)

1. There was a chance the player could accidentally skip the dialogue that triggered Slim and Frank coming to camp. I have changed the trigger for that so they should spawn in for anyone that has completed a horseshoe game.  I also added a backup trigger to the horseshoe game for one bug report where a player was stuck there, hopefully that solves their issue.

2. There was a crash that would sometimes happen on spawning deer due to a math problem with the spawn chances. I have fixed the error I found which will hopefully cause those crashes to stop. Keeping my eye on that one.

3. Albino deer hit animation - the albino deer was drawing from the pie bald object when hit so it wasn't running wounded like it should. I believe this also caused some crashes on a successful Albino kill because the animal would just keep running instead of staying on screen. It would then get destroyed and the game wouldn't be able to access its code.

4. The spawn rate of the Albinos was also drawing from the pie bald numbers which meant a much greater chance of spawning them, and them spawning earlier in the deer meter than they should. They will now only spawn when the meter is full, and have a 10% chance of spawning.

5. When I was making changes tonight the fishing camera got messed up and then I realized it was actually kind of cool. The camera now zooms in a bit and follows the fishing lure. I really like elements of it because it adds some weight and action to the fishing. However, the one thing I'm not sure about is the camera is a little jumpy when bringing the lure up near the surface without a fish on. I'm open to feedback on that when people have tried it out.

That's all for tonight. I need to mark essays now. Oof.

notes.title: Hotfix: March 6
notes.content:
Two bugs fixed in this one:

1. Albino deer kills not registering. Everything should be working normally now. Please let me know if they are not.

2. Fixed a graphical issue with the deer meter going outside of its frame.

More to come!

notes.title: Hotfix: March 5
notes.content:
Some quality of life changes and a bugfix:

1. Added an option to have indicators for climbing trees while in map mode. This is on by default. When you open the map you will now see a green indicator under trees that can be climbed and bushes that can have a blind.

2. Extended the view distance while in a treestand. When a player enters a stand the view will now zoom out to provide a greater window for both shooting and scouting.

3. Changed deer behaviour that was resulting in a graphical error. Deer used to bounce into each other and this would cause flickering or them to hang up. Now deer can pass through each other. This also means that deer can be stacked on screen. When this happens the first deer hit by a bullet will be killed so be careful if there is a specific buck you're aiming at and they are stacked with a doe.

I've also been working on a free hunt mode due to popular request. This is a map that's 4 times the size though it is not randomized (it wouldn't be too difficult to make some more of these for variety though). This would include all animals, though the deer behaviour will need to be scaled down slightly due to logistics. I should be able to have this out in a beta form in game quite soon.

notes.title: Hotfix: March 2
notes.content:
[list]
[*]  Quail hunting NPCs will no longer shoot birds that aren't on screen.

[*]  Changed the point values of bucks in the deer hunts. Currently it was too difficult to climb up the deer hunting point system. Now does give 1 point, button buck 5, spike 7, shooter 10, trophy 15, piebald 25, albino 50. This should make getting skunked a little less severe and a little more palatable.

[*]  Changed the money (which was obsolete) in the arcade game to a clock. Clocks drop randomly from shot animals and when picked up will add 3 seconds on to the timer. This will make some of the achievements a little easier to get, though the decision to shoot or run after the timer addition remains with the player.
[/list]

notes.title: Quick Fix:
notes.content:
- Fixed potential issue where player would get stuck on the go hunt with Mutt stage of the intro steps

- Toned down the range and speed at which the quail hunt NPCs fire. (Will also soon update to make it so they do not shoot birds off screen)

notes.title: CHANGES AND FIXES
notes.content:
Between the playtest and some keys going out I'm getting lots of great feedback and have been busy making changes. Here are some of the fixes that have been recently implemented:

Changelog:

1. Quick hunt now starts at 11am. Deer are already bedded for the morning. This means the player has ample time to scout the map and set up without worrying about bumping into a deer. This seemed to be the best solution. I found when I played I’d just fast forward time until they were in bed anyways.

2. Deer should no longer accidentally spook during map creation or entry point selection.

3. Put in autosave functionality after key events so as to not lose progress on a crash.

4. Frank and Slim unlocked just from playing horseshoes (no win required).

5. Fixed fishing crash when clicking right mouse button if certain weapons were previously equipped.

6. Added quest marker to shotgun in cabin to improve visibility for player.

7. Fixed a problem where deer tracks weren’t invisible while in the map mode.

8. Fixed a bug that could cause crash on map generation of quick hunts.

9. Defaulted off the ironsight zoom (going to change the zoom function to make it less finicky in the near future).

Next Step:

Streamlining tutorial #2 to improve clarity of instructions / make sure all info is acquired

notes.title: End of Playtest
notes.content:
The playest is now over and I just want to thank everyone who participated. The feedback I received was extremely valuable in making quality of life fixes and squashing bugs. As a result there is a pretty tidy demo ready to go for steam nextfest. It wouldn't have been possible without your help and I am very grateful.

- James

notes.title: Progress Update and Roadmap.
notes.content:
[b]Hi Hunters![/b]

Just wanted to give an update on the game's progress and a window into where the game is headed.

First, the biggest news: Public Land Hunter will be participating in steam's NEXT FEST in February. This will provide players with an opportunity to play the game's demo, after which the game will be released shortly after (aiming for a FEB 16th)!  *Note I'll be looking for players to beta test the demo before the festival.

Next bit of news is what I have been working on:

After a brief development hiatus due to some family health concerns I've gotten back into working on the game and have been focusing on adding variety. One of the things I noticed in Alpha gameplay was that a lot of the hunts felt quite similar. I believe this has often been an issue with hunting games (even the ones I love) and I really want to avoid his in PLH. As such, I've reworked some of the hunts to give them their own unique mechanics and feel. While this comes at the cost of some realism, I think it ultimately makes the game a lot more fun to play. I still want to keep the deer hunting as much of a simulation as possible as that to me is the heart of the game, but the new mechanics in some of the other hunts keep things interesting.

I've also looked to add some variety through the various mini games that the player can do around camp. I'd already worked out a horseshoe game the player can compete in and am currently putting the finishing touches on a fishing game. These sorts of activities serve a dual purpose for the player: 1. It will be an avenue for unlocks like cosmetics and new friends at the hunt camp 2. It provides variety from the standard hunting gameplay loop. I suppose as a third bonus it also helps build character and relationships with the members of the hunt camp.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42751278/f151ce3a251212f7a844b019a65ca29575f60fb0.png[/img]

Lastly I wanted to post a roadmap of what is currently in the game and what I'd like to add before release (or for free after release if any of the features don't make in by Feb).

[b]Current features:[/b]

[b]Hunt camp: [/b]a base of operations for the player where they can play mini games, unlock hunts and meet npcs who will give missions and compete in challenges.

[b]Hunter’s cabin: [/b]a place where players can unlock weapons and upgrades, see high scores and play the dysentery trail arcade game for more unlocks.

[b]Randomized maps:[/b] all hunts are programmed to take place on randomized maps to make hunts unique and increase replayability.

[b]Seasons:[/b] hunts take place in either summer, fall or winter. Seasons affect the aesthetic and the mechanics of the hunt. Tracks are left in snow, fall leaves crunch under foot and summer foliage provides lots of cover.

[b]Weapons: [/b]currently the player has access to a .22 varmint rifle, shotgun, recurve bow, assault rifle, .308 scoped rifle.

[b]Animals: [/b]each of the animals has their own unique AI and mechanics to add variety to the hunts. Rabbits are plentiful and graze in the fields near the tall grass. They will scatter if the player gets too close or at the sound of gunfire. Grouse lurk in the thick stuff and need to be driven out by the player or a dog before getting a shot opportunity. Ducks need to be called in with a rhythm game before a shot opportunity presents itself. Feral pigs storm farm fields in the night and need to be culled  before all the crops are destroyed. Deer follow a realistic pattern of feeding at dusk and dawn and sleeping during the day. With most weapons they will need to be scouted, patterned and ambushed for a successful hunt.

[b]Camp friends:[/b] there are currently five npcs who will join the hunt camp as the player progresses. These camp friends provide missions, unlocks and competitions for the player.

[b]Mini games:[/b] horseshoes and fishing currently give the player a chance to take a break from hunting and compete against the other members of the hunt camp for cosmetics and hunter upgrades.

[b]Planned features:[/b]

[b]More animals:[/b] I’d like to add more animals to the game, keeping with the idea that each hunt should have its own unique mechanics. Planned animals include turkeys, bears, coyotes and goats.

[b]More weapons:[/b] compound bow, muzzle loader and a spear are in the works.

[b]More biomes:[/b] desert and alpine hunts are high on the list.

[b]More camp friends:[/b] each animal has an associated camp friend so I’d look to add a new one for each new animal.

[b]More mini games:[/b] more friends means more games. Things like skeet shooting, axe throwing and tube racing down the creek.

[b]Fishing:[/b] a fly fishing variant for the fishing mini game.


And that's all for now. Hopefully this gives you an idea of what's in store for PLH and I'm getting very excited for people to finally have a chance at playing it! I look forward to seeing you all in camp!
